issues.legal_issue: Using land leased for keeping vehicles as a garage to build structures and maintain the vehicles does not amount to using the land for a purpose other than the purpose of the lease.
material_facts: The land was leased on a condition that it be used for keeping lorries as a garage.
The tenant erected structures and used the land for keeping and maintaining lorries, including workshop work.
issues.conclusion: The tenant's construction and workshop use for maintaining the lorries were consistent with the leased purpose and did not attract the prohibition on using leased property for another purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 108(o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, which bars use for a purpose other than the one for which property was leased. It construed keeping vehicles as a garage in its ordinary sense, including housing or tending to vehicles, and concluded that the described workshop use was within that purpose. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_suit: The dispute is an appeal arising from a suit seeking eviction from leased land.
predicates.land_leased_for_vehicle_garage: The landlord leased the land for keeping vehicles as a garage.
predicates.tenant_uses_land_to_house_and_maintain_v: The tenant uses the land to house vehicles and carry out work to maintain them.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns land leased as a vehicle garage and used by the tenant to house and maintain vehicles, that use is treated as within the leased purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who otherwise meets the statutory definition of a thika tenant need not obtain the landlord's prior permission to erect a structure on the land to qualify as a thika tenant.
material_facts: The tenant held the land under a landlord and was liable to pay rent.
The tenant erected structures on the land for the tenant's transport business.
The statutory definition required a tenant to have erected or acquired a structure for a residential, manufacturing, or business purpose but did not mention landlord consent.
issues.conclusion: The tenant qualified as a thika tenant without proving prior permission or consent from the landlord to erect the structures.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 2(5) of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act, 1949. Because that definition contains no requirement of landlord consent, the Court refused to read one into it. It treated the Act as beneficial legislation conferring rights on tenants and held that a restriction could not be introduced by judicial interpretation without express words or necessary manifest intendment. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.proceeding_determines_thika_tenant_statu: The proceeding requires the court to determine whether a person qualifies as a thika tenant.
predicates.tenant_holds_land_under_another_for_rent: The person holds land under another person and is liable to pay rent for it.
predicates.tenant_erected_or_acquired_structure_for: The person erected or acquired a structure on the land for a business purpose.

issues.definition: When a status proceeding concerns a rent-paying landholder who erected or acquired a business structure on the land, the person may qualify as a thika tenant without landlord consent.
